title: Szedłem → przyszedłem
note: Block 3 payoff unit (B1-SPINE). b1_past_isc closed on a promise -- 'two more everyday verbs, coming very soon, are built on exactly these shapes' -- and slide 1 delivers it by name: przyjść and wyjść are the szedł table with przy-/wy- welded on the front, nothing else changed. Four verbs as two arrive/leave pairs: przyjść/wyjść on the suppletive stems (14 past forms, taught whole via the mirror table), przyjechać/wyjechać on the regular -ać rule owned since a2_past_ac (14 forms, rule-derived, near-zero cost). SINGULAR ONLY throughout, both genders in production with (m)/(f) cues; plural past is virile territory and stays fenced. FUTURES taught (b1_perf_future precedes): framed exactly as that unit framed kupię -- a verb for a single finished event has no present, so its present-shaped forms mean the future -- and its wypiję = wy + piję move is reused literally: przyjadę = przy + jadę, przyjdę = przy + idę (i→j). PERSONS CALL, logged: futures in the three SINGULAR persons only (ja/ty/on·ona) = 12 forms. Reasons: (a) the unit is singular-only in the past by design -- one consistent frame; (b) plural futures pull toward 3pl subjects while oni/one stay fenced until b1_virile_past; (c) the unit already carries 28 past forms and load-splitting says stop. The plural endings will cost nothing later once the virile block lands. The je-/jad- split in przyjadę/przyjedziesz is shown as a table fact inherited from jadę/jedziesz (a2_jechac precedent), never a rule. ASPECT: no imperfective counterparts appear or are alluded to anywhere; arrive/leave are framed as events that happen once ('an arrival is like kupiłem -- once, and it is done'), glossed plain simple past (came/arrived/left) and plain future (will come), per the AGENTS gloss rules -- nothing to un-teach when the imperfective family eventually arrives. DIRECTION MAPPING kept deliberately clean: przy- always with do + genitive destinations, wy- always with z + genitive sources -- all verified pooled chunks taught AS destination/source (do domu/pracy/miasta/szkoły/biura from a1 do-units; z domu/z pracy/z miasta/z biura/ze sklepu from a1_prep_do_z + a1_prep_review_2). The real-Polish pattern 'wyjechać do + place' (left FOR somewhere) is deliberately not shown -- true, but it would blur the przy-=to / wy-=from picture on first contact. FENCED, absent from this file: po-/do-/prze-/za- prefixes; przychodzić-family imperfectives (wychodzę/wychodzisz sit in the pool from an earlier routine pack and are deliberately never used or mentioned here); plural past; oni/one; conditional; będę (does not occur at all -- the two-futures contrast belongs to b1_two_futures and is not re-opened). HOMOGRAPHS / check_new.py run on all candidates: przyjść ALREADY TAUGHT (trunk_can_a1, as the infinitive 'to come' in Mogę przyjść jutro -- same word, same function; recycled not re-taught, and used as the slide-1 callback); all 40 inflected forms plus wyjść/przyjechać/wyjechać verified NEW, zero collisions. 'w przyszłym tygodniu' (pooled, b1_plans) deliberately AVOIDED so the only przysz- string in this unit's tasks means 'came' -- 'next week' meanings are carried by jutro / w weekend instead; do Polski and do Anglii avoided (polski/anglii pooled as adjective/locative -- different function would evade the string check); pociągiem/autobusem recycled as the instrumentals a2_inst_transport taught them as; późno/wcześnie/rano/o drugiej/w zeszłym tygodniu/w weekend all pooled in exactly the functions used. FORKS: (a) Dopasuj = 12 bare forms covering all four verbs, both tenses, both genders -- the form supply is ample, so no sentence rows are needed for balance; (b) intro-table-only forms (2sg pasts of the vehicle pair, the neuter pasts, przyjedziesz/wyjadę among the futures) are tagged in teaches_lemmas per the b1_perf_future precedent so later units may draw on them -- the production core is 1sg/3sg in both genders plus the ja-futures; (c) quiz distractors are real taught strings only, no invented wrong forms; (d) the three new infinitives are taught via the intro (the -ać rule slide needs them) and tagged, not drilled in type -- matching the b1_past_isc treatment of iść.

intro.title: The promise, kept
intro.body:
Last unit ended with a promise: two more everyday verbs are built on exactly the szedł shapes. Here they are.

przyjść — to come, to arrive. You have known this word since A1: Mogę przyjść jutro.
wyjść — to go out, to leave.

Both are iść with a piece welded onto the front. przy- points toward — you arrive. wy- points out — you leave. Their past is the table you just learned, with the prefix in front and not one letter changed behind it.
intro.body_pl: przy- + szedł / szła = przyszedł / przyszła. wy- + szedł / szła = wyszedł / wyszła.

intro.title: An arrival happens once
intro.body:
szedłem says you were on the way — the walking itself, still in motion. przyszedłem says you got there — the arrival. An arrival is like kupiłem: it happens once and it is done. That is why the glosses are plain: I came, I left — not 'I was coming'.

After przy-, the destination you know: do + genitive. After wy-, the starting point: z + genitive — the from-phrases you have used since A1: z domu, z pracy, ze sklepu.
intro.body_pl: szedłem = jeszcze w ruchu. przyszedłem = raz i gotowe. Po przy-: do + dopełniacz. Po wy-: z + dopełniacz.

examples.en: Yesterday I was going to work. (m — on the way)
I came to work early. (m — arrived, done)
I left the house in the morning. (m)
Mum came out of the shop.

intro.title: By vehicle: przyjechać and wyjechać
intro.body:
The same two prefixes fit onto jechać. przyjechać — to arrive by vehicle. wyjechać — to leave by vehicle, to go away.

No new table to memorise here. These two take the regular past rule you have used since mieszkał: drop the -ć, add -ł, add the endings you know — przyjechać → przyjechał, wyjechać → wyjechał.
intro.body_pl: Zasada z -ać: przyjechać → przyjechał, wyjechać → wyjechał.

intro.title: Feet or wheels — the old choice, in the past
intro.body:
Idę czy jadę? made you choose feet or wheels every time. The past asks the same question:

On foot → przyszedłem, wyszedłem.
By vehicle → przyjechałem, wyjechałem.

Across town on the bus — przyjechałem. Out of the office on your own two feet — wyszedłem. Only the vehicle decides, exactly as it did with idę and jadę.
intro.body_pl: Pieszo: przyszedłem, wyszedłem. Pojazdem: przyjechałem, wyjechałem.

examples.en: Anna arrived in the city yesterday. (by train)
The child came to school late. (on foot)

intro.title: The future: przyjdę, wyjdę
intro.body:
przyjść and wyjść name a single finished event — so, exactly like kupić, they have no present tense, and their present-shaped forms mean the future. You have made this move before: piję → wypiję. Now the same thing happens to idę:

przy + idę → przyjdę — I will come. The i turns into j, and that is the whole change.
wy + idę → wyjdę — I will go out, I will leave.

Read the three persons off the table — the endings are the ones idę and idziesz have carried since A1.
intro.body_pl: idę → przyjdę / wyjdę. Forma jak teraźniejsza, znaczenie: przyszłość — jak kupię.

intro.title: przyjadę, wyjadę — and no gender
intro.body:
By vehicle the future is even more familiar: przyjadę is literally przy + jadę, and wyjadę is wy + jadę. The whole jechać pattern comes along with it, including the ja- / je- swap you know from jadę, jedziesz, jedzie — read it off the table, nothing to work out.

And one relief carried over from kupię: the future keeps no gender. In the past you choose przyszedłem or przyszłam. In the future a man says przyjdę and a woman says przyjdę.
intro.body_pl: jadę → przyjadę / wyjadę. Przyszłość bez rodzaju: przyjdę — mężczyzna i kobieta tak samo.

examples.en: Grandma will arrive at the weekend. (by car)
The train will arrive at two.
When will you come to the office? (on foot)

quiz.explain: tata is a he, and the masculine forms keep the szed- shape with przy- in front: przyszedł. przyszedłem would put you in the sentence instead of dad.
mama is feminine, so the short sz- shape with -a: wyszła. The szed- shapes belong to the masculine forms only — exactly as in the szedł table.
pociągiem — by train, so wheels: przyjechała. przyszła would mean she walked in. wyjechała points the wrong way — out, not toward.

quiz.prompt: still on the way, not there yet (m) →
quiz.explain: szedłem is the journey itself, still in motion. przyszedłem is the moment it ends — you are there. That contrast is the whole difference between last unit and this one.

quiz.prompt: Jutro ___ do biura rano. (ja, on foot)
quiz.explain: jutro points forwards, so the past przyszedłem is out. On foot, so not przyjadę. And przyjdzie is he or she — the ja-form keeps the -ę.

quiz.prompt: When will you leave work? (to a man)
quiz.explain: will leave points forwards: wyjdziesz — wy + idziesz. wyszedłeś already happened, wyjdzie asks about him, and wyjadę asks about me.

quiz.prompt: Babcia ___ w weekend. (she will — by car)
quiz.explain: By car, so the jechać family — and babcia is a she, so przyjedzie, the je- middle of the table. przyjdzie would have her walking the whole way.
tata is a he, and the he-form keeps the szed- shape and stops at the -ł: wyszedł. wyszła is his wife's word.
pociąg is a he in Polish, and it has wheels — przyjedzie. wyjedzie is the wrong direction: that train is leaving.

quiz.prompt: Mój brat ___ z miasta w zeszłym tygodniu. (went away)
quiz.explain: z miasta — out of the city, so wy-. Leaving a whole city is a wheels-scale journey: wyjechał, the regular -ał past of wyjechać.

quiz.prompt: I will come tomorrow (on foot) — a woman speaking →
quiz.explain: The future keeps no gender — przyjdę for a man and for a woman alike. przyszłam is the past, where the gender choice still lives.

type_items.explain: przy- welded onto szedłem — the very table you learned last unit, doing its promised second job.
The feminine forms keep their short sz- shape: przy + szłam.
wy- points out — same szedłem behind it, only the prefix changes the direction.
Regular -ać past, the mieszkał rule: przyjecha- + ł + em. No table to memorise on the vehicle side.
przy + idę, with the i turned into j. A present-shaped form on one of these verbs means the future — the kupię rule.
Literally przy + jadę. The word you have said since Idę czy jadę?, pointed at tomorrow.
The je- middle of the jechać table carries over: jedzie → przyjedzie. One form for he and for she — no gender in the future.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Dad came home late. (on foot)
Type: Mum left the house in the morning. (on foot)
use_items.explain: wy- takes the starting point, and the starting point stands in the genitive after z: z domu — the from-phrase you have owned since A1.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Yesterday I came to work early. (m, on foot)
Type: Anna arrived in the city yesterday. (by vehicle)
Type: I came to work by bus. (f)
use_items.explain: autobusem answers how, so the verb must be from the jechać family — przyjechałam, not przyszłam. Feet and a bus cannot share a sentence.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My brother left the city last week. (by vehicle)
use_items.answer: Mój brat wyjechał z miasta w zeszłym tygodniu.
accepts: Mój brat wyjechał z miasta w zeszłym tygodniu.
Mój brat wyjechał z miasta w zeszłym tygodniu
W zeszłym tygodniu mój brat wyjechał z miasta.
W zeszłym tygodniu mój brat wyjechał z miasta

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The child came to school late. (on foot)
use_items.explain: dziecko is neuter, so the -o ending on the short sz- shape: przyszło — the same -o as szło and było.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The train will arrive at two.
Type: Grandma will arrive at the weekend. (by car)
use_items.explain: przyjedzie for babcia and przyjedzie for dziadek — the future keeps no gender, so the subject costs you nothing here.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Tomorrow I will leave the office early. (on foot)
Type: When will you come to the office? (on foot)
